guard: every ordinary user-auth broker connection receives its own trusted-provisioned fixed-rail public-KV watcher pair before admission, so overlapping commands have complete independent snapshots and one graceful stop cannot delete another connection's consumers
command: corepack pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && corepack pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/auth build && PATH=/workspace/state/tools/nats-server-v2.12.12-b:$PATH corepack pnpm smoke:user-spawn:live
why: Interactive CLI bearers use the agent profile's trusted-pinned public-KV watch rails even
though their presentation card is an endpoint. The auth callout knows the validated client
inbox nonce before it releases the broker JWT, so it derives a bounded connection UID and
uses the ephemeral provisioner to create that connection's exact pair. Distinct commands must
not collapse back to one lifecycle-owned pair: a second live process needs its own complete
LastPerSubject snapshot, and predecessor stop may delete only predecessor resources.

mutations.name: collapse every user-auth connection back onto one shared watcher uid
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: an overlapping successor binds a distinct, complete watcher pair while the predecessor stays live
mutations.cell: an overlapping successor binds a distinct, complete watcher pair while the predecessor stays live
mutations.afterRestore: corepack pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && corepack pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/auth build
